hero.title: Our Story: A Journey of Resilience
hero.description: The Children of Shingwauk Alumni Association (CSAA) is a dedicated non-profit volunteer organization representing the survivors of the Shingwauk and Wawanosh Indian Residential Schools. We stand as a testament to endurance, a bridge to history, and a community for those who walked these grounds.

mission.title: Mission & Vision
mission.body1: Our primary mission is to ensure the history of the residential school system is never forgotten, while providing a safe space for survivors to find support, shared understanding, and a collective voice.
mission.body2: We envision a future where healing is facilitated through education, the preservation of archives, and the creation of lasting memorials that honor the dignity of every student who attended these institutions.
mission.imageAlt: A serene close-up of indigenous beadwork on natural cedar bark

legacy.title: Explore Our Legacy
legacy.description: Connecting the past to the present through history, healing, and documentation.

csaaLegacy.title: The CSAA Legacy
csaaLegacy.description: Learn about the formation of our association and the pioneers who fought to preserve our shared history.

healingMemorials.title: Healing & Memorials
healingMemorials.description: Discover sacred sites like Crying Rock and the Wawanosh memorials that serve as focal points for reflection.

archives.title: Research & Archives
archives.description: We are committed to safeguarding documents, photographs, and oral histories for future generations.

origins.label: 1873 — Origins
origins.body: The Shingwauk Home opened its doors, originally envisioned as an industrial school. Over the decades, it became a central site in the residential school system.

closure.label: 1970 — Closure
closure.body: The Shingwauk Indian Residential School officially closed, marking the end of a painful era and the beginning of a long path toward reclamation.

reunion.label: 1981 — First Reunion
reunion.body: Survivors gathered for the first time as an organized group, leading to the formal creation of the Alumni Association to support one another.

today.label: Today — Active Advocacy
today.body: The CSAA remains a vibrant force, working alongside Algoma University and the Shingwauk Residential Schools Centre to educate and heal.

dedication.quote: "We honor the children who were taken, the parents who were left behind, and the survivors who carried the weight of history. To those who did not return, your memory is our sacred fire; to those who remain, your resilience is our light. We walk this path of healing together, today and for all generations to come."

hero.title: Healing & Memorials
hero.description: We honor the resilience and spirit of the Children of Shingwauk. This sacred space is dedicated to healing, remembrance, and the enduring legacy of our Alumni. Through shared stories and hallowed grounds, we walk together on the path toward reconciliation.

inMemorial.title: In Memorial
inMemorial.description: Honoring the memory of those we have lost. This dedicated space provides a permanent tribute for families and the community to share remembrance and stories of loved ones.

exhibition.title: Shingwauk Hall Exhibition
exhibition.description: Explore the physical and virtual exhibition documenting the lived experiences and historical reality of Shingwauk Hall and its students.

everyChild.title: Every Child Matters
everyChild.description: Join the movement for truth and reconciliation. Understanding the profound impact of the residential school system on generations of indigenous families.

cryingRock.title: Crying Rock
cryingRock.description: Discover the spiritual significance of the Crying Rock, a place of historical reflection and deep connection for the Shingwauk community.

wawnosh.title: Wawanosh Memorial Project
wawnosh.description: Honouring the legacy of the Wawanosh Indian Residential School. This project preserves the stories, names, and memories of those whose lives were shaped by this institution.

support.title: Support Our Healing Journey
support.description: The Children of Shingwauk Alumni Association relies on your support to maintain these memorials and continue our archival work.
